answer: One concrete defense is to anchor each agent identity to a refundable economic stake that is slashed on misbehavior. Minting a new identity then costs real capital, so a sybil flood from one actor on some obscure knoll of the network becomes prohibitively expensive. Peers also watch a continuous activity pulse: genuine agents accrue a signed history of honest work over time, while freshly spun-up clones have no such record and are throttled until they earn it.
